title: Observable- and state-selective prethermalization and bounds on prethermal lifetimes
authors: C. L. Sriram, Soumya Kanti Pal, Lea F. Santos
abstract: Prethermalization describes long-lived intermediate regimes that precede equilibrium and can dominate experimentally accessible dynamics. Here, we show that a separation of spectral energy scales, despite giving rise to a hierarchy of dynamical timescales, does not by itself guarantee the appearance of a prethermal plateau. Under the same Hamiltonian, some observables may exhibit prethermal behavior, while others relax directly toward equilibrium. We uncover the mechanism governing this selectivity, showing that the emergence of a prethermal plateau depends not only on the Hamiltonian, but also on the observable and the initial state. Our results apply broadly to systems close to a fully permutation-symmetric limit and are illustrated with a long-range interacting spin model. We further prove that the Loschmidt echo provides a lower bound on the prethermal lifetime of any bounded observable whenever the prethermal and exact dynamics are unitary.
summary: This theoretical paper establishes that prethermalization is an observable- and state-selective phenomenon, meaning not all physical quantities will exhibit a long-lived plateau even if the Hamiltonian suggests it. Crucially, the authors derive a general lower bound on this prethermal lifetime using the Loschmidt echo, providing a powerful diagnostic tool for characterizing non-equilibrium dynamics in quantum many-body systems.
main_problem: The paper investigates the conditions under which prethermalization occurs in quantum many-body systems, specifically addressing whether separated energy scales guarantee a prethermal plateau for all observables.
main_result: Prethermalization is highly selective; its existence depends on the specific observable and the initial state, not just the Hamiltonian structure. Furthermore, the Loschmidt echo provides a general lower bound on the prethermal lifetime for any bounded observable.
method: The authors use theoretical analysis involving Hamiltonian perturbation theory, analyzing matrix elements in the energy eigenbasis, and deriving bounds using the trace-norm inequality applied to the Loschmidt echo and Uhlmann fidelity.
model_or_system: The analysis is applied to long-range interacting spin models, exemplified by a 1D transverse field Ising model with power-law interactions ($\hat{H}(\alpha)$). The dynamics are studied in the presence of a small perturbation ($\hat{H} = \hat{H}_0 + \epsilon \hat{V}$).
key_observables: Prethermal plateau visibility, entanglement entropy ($S_{	ext{Ent}}$), total magnetization ($M_z$), first moment of excitation density ($C_z$), Loschmidt echo ($L(t)$), and Uhlmann fidelity ($F(t)$).
important_parameters: Interaction-range exponent ($\alpha$), perturbation strength ($\epsilon$), and time scales relative to $\epsilon^{-1}$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the perturbation strength $\epsilon$ being small and the time $t$ being short relative to the inverse perturbation strength ($t \ll \epsilon^{-1}$).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the comparison of time evolution for different observables ($S_{	ext{Ent}}$ vs. $M_z$) showing selectivity, and demonstrate the mathematical bound relating the observable deviation to the Loschmidt echo departure.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the general framework of prethermalization in weakly perturbed systems. It then analyzes the role of symmetry (permutation invariance) in suppressing plateaus for certain observables. Finally, it derives and applies the rigorous bound using the Loschmidt echo and fidelity to quantify the minimum prethermal lifetime.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous, quantitative tools (like the Loschmidt echo bound) to predict the duration of non-equilibrium dynamics, which is crucial for designing experiments that probe intermediate quantum phases.
